title: Trust Task specification — front matter meta-schema
description: Shape of the YAML front matter that every specs/<slug>/<version>/spec.md must declare. Mirrors the declarations required by SPEC.md §7.3.

slug.description: Lowercase, hyphen-separated short name; may be organized into one or more `/`-delimited path segments (e.g. `acl/grant`). Each segment satisfies the single-segment grammar. The slug `trust-task` and any slug whose first segment is `trust-task` or begins with `trust-task-` are reserved per SPEC §6.1; only the framework-defined slugs `trust-task`, `trust-task-error`, `trust-task-ok`, `trust-task-next-step`, and `trust-task-discovery` may use the reserved namespace (the registry hosts those itself). The slug MUST match the relative folder path from `specs/` to the version directory's parent.

version.description: MAJOR.MINOR per SPEC §5.1; matches the version-segment folder name.

summary.description: One-sentence elevator pitch shown on registry cards and as the page lede.

status.description: Lifecycle status per SPEC §5.3. `retired` is terminal; a retired spec SHOULD declare `supersededBy`.

targetFrameworkVersion.description: Framework MAJOR.MINOR this spec targets, per SPEC §7.3 item 3.

category.description:
TT_CATEGORIES id. Pick the one that most cleanly describes the task's domain. Roughly:
- access-control: ACL / role / permission / capability tasks (acl/*).
- ai-agents: tasks specific to AI-agent interaction patterns.
- authentication: login, session, challenge/response, passkey, step-up (auth/*, confirm/*).
- chat: conversational messaging between agents and messaging-platform bridges, signed and chained for non-repudiation (chat/*).
- consent: authorization-to-proceed tasks that gate whether an interaction (a connection / channel / group / conversation) may reach a protected party such as an AI agent, with operator/approver consent on first contact (consent/*).
- credentials: vault / credential management (vault/*).
- data-exchange: data-transport / sync / event-stream tasks (sync/*).
- did-management: DID lifecycle, hosting, domain, server registry (did-management/*).
- framework: framework-defined meta-tasks (trust-task-error, trust-task-discovery, etc.).
- governance: policy / rule-engine / decision tasks (policy/*).
- identity: identity-anchor / device-binding / persona tasks (device/*).
- key-management: custody and lifecycle of cryptographic key material held on a producer's behalf — creation, import, listing, rename, revocation, and the signing-oracle surface that exercises a key without ever exporting it (keys/*). Distinct from credentials, which is about stored secrets and credentials rather than the keys that sign.
- messaging: messaging-infrastructure operation of a mediator / relay — account and ACL administration, liveness/health ping, and other operator-facing control of the message-transport substrate itself, as distinct from the application-level access-control of acl/* (messaging/*).
- notifications: push wake-up control plane — register a push channel, provision the trigger allowlist, request a contentless wake (push/*).
- payments: payment-flow tasks.
- reputation: reputation / attestation tasks.

Enforced as a closed enum to prevent the silent category drift that produced `permission` (now access-control) and `did-management` (recognised) — adding a new category is now a deliberate spec-meta-schema PR rather than a typo in a single spec.md.

keywords.description: Free-text keywords used by registry search.

authors.description: Editor names or working group attributions.

member.description: Which framework document member (SPEC §4.8) this party fills, when it maps to one. Omit for a party that is named in the payload but is neither the document's `issuer` nor its `recipient`. At most one party may declare `member: issuer` and at most one `member: recipient`. A party declared `member: recipient` with `requirement: REQUIRED` obliges consumers to reject a document lacking an in-band `recipient` (SPEC §7.2 item 5).

parties.description: Roles expected in a conforming document, per SPEC §7.3 item 5. VID scheme acceptance is a per-consumer trust-framework concern and is deliberately not constrained here.

level.description: How much a successful execution changes at the recipient. `none`: read-only / idempotent probe, no persisted state change (list, get, check-name, discovery). `mutating`: creates or alters recoverable state (publish a log entry, grant a role, register a device). `destructive`: irreversible or authority-shifting (deactivate a DID, rotate the only update key, delete, change-owner, wipe a device).

rationale.description: Why this level. For `destructive`, name the irreversible effect a human is consenting to.

sideEffects.description: Descriptive classification of the recipient-side effect of successful execution, per SPEC.md §7.3 item 13. DESCRIPTIVE, NOT PRESCRIPTIVE: it states what the task does, never whether approval is required — a specification MUST NOT declare a consent/approval/step-up requirement, as that policy belongs to the consumer and MUST NOT be delegable to the registry. A consumer enforcing an approval policy MUST derive the authoritative level from the handler it is about to invoke, and MUST treat an absent/unrecognized declaration as no weaker than `mutating`. Required of every conforming spec; `none` is the correct value for read-only and framework-plumbing tasks.

consequences.description: Human-facing second-order effects a consent surface SHOULD surface alongside the primary action — the effects a naive payload diff would miss because they live in the handler's semantics, not the payload's shape (e.g. 'Any document change also rotates this DID's update keys'). Static fallback text; a live executor MAY instead compute a per-request effects list by dry-running the real handler.

subjectPath.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer locating the subject identifier (usually a DID) inside the payload — e.g. `/did`. Lets a delegated-execution PEP answer 'does the executing agent speak for this subject?' declaratively rather than with per-task code. Omit for tasks with no single subject (discovery, list, whoami).

discloses.description: Sensitivity of data returned to the caller. `none`: an acknowledgement or determination only. `metadata`: non-secret descriptive data about a subject or resource (an enumeration, a status read). `secret`: confidential material the caller retains (released credential material, a usable session blob).

actsAsSubject.description: True when execution exercises the subject's own authority to produce an attributable effect in their name — a login on their behalf, a signature bearing their identity, a credential issued under their authority — even when nothing is disclosed and no recipient state changes.

rationale.description: Names the disclosed material or the exercised authority. Required when `discloses` is `secret` or `actsAsSubject` is true.

exposure.description: Exposure class per SPEC.md §7.3 item 14 — the confidentiality-and-agency dimension, orthogonal to the integrity-focused `sideEffects` of item 13. States what leaves the recipient (`discloses`) and whether the subject's authority is exercised (`actsAsSubject`), independent of any state change. DESCRIPTIVE, NOT PRESCRIPTIVE, on the same terms as `sideEffects`: a consumer MUST derive authoritative values from the handler it invokes and MUST treat an absent declaration as no less exposed than `discloses: secret` with `actsAsSubject: true`.

code.description: Namespaced code per SPEC §8.5, e.g. 'kyc-handoff:documentRevoked' (framework 0.2 lowerCamelCase, SPEC §4.10) or 'acl/grant:permission_denied' (frozen 0.1 snake_case). The local part accepts both casings so 0.1 and 0.2 specs validate against the same schema. The namespace before the colon MUST be either the spec's own slug, or a family namespace — a proper path prefix of that slug, for a code whose meaning is defined once for the whole family in a shared convention (e.g. 'did-management:unknownDomain' on 'did-management/did/delete'). This pattern checks the grammar only; the prefix relationship is enforced by checkErrorCodeNamespaces() in scripts/build-registry.mjs, because JSON Schema cannot compare one property against another.

detailsSchema.description: Optional JSON Schema fragment describing the shape of the error's details object.

errorCodes.description: Task-specific error codes per SPEC §7.3 item 9. Omit or leave empty if none.

jsonLdContext.description: Set to true if a context.jsonld file sits alongside spec.md. Per SPEC §7.3 item 10.

related.description: Slugs of related Trust Tasks; hierarchical slugs use `/` separators (e.g. `acl/grant`).

method.description: Value of a method-discriminator field in the payload (e.g. `payload.method`) that activates this extension. For did-management/* specs, this is the DID method identifier (e.g. `webvh`, `web`).

schema.description: Slug of the shared schema that documents the extension shape. Must match a discovered shared schema (file under an `_`-prefixed directory). The build script validates this resolves.

requirement.description: How strongly producers should populate this extension when their `method` matches. Default OPTIONAL — extension is purely advisory metadata.

methodExtensions.description: Method-discriminated extensions a producer MAY (or SHOULD/MUST per `requirement`) include in `ext` when their payload selects the named `method`. Each entry pins a shared schema by slug; the registry build surfaces it in the spec's Uses panel and links the schema page. Unlike $ref-resolved dependencies, method extensions aren't structurally required by the payload schema — they're an out-of-band convention for vendor-namespaced ext data.

knownImplementations.description: URLs (repositories, products, deployment documentation) of implementations known to produce or consume this task. Informative, not exhaustive: it lets registry readers distinguish adopted specifications from proposals, and doubles as evidence toward the draft → candidate transition (SPEC §5.3). Omit when no implementation is known.

wireCompatibleWith.description: Declares that this version is wire-identical to the named earlier version of the same slug, modulo the mechanical normalizations of SPEC §4.10 — casing of member names and enumerated values — and framework/shared-schema `$ref` re-pins. Advisory: consumers MAY dual-accept documents of the named version by normalizing casing and retyping the URI, without a hand-written adapter. New versions should not need this field — editorial changes to a `draft` spec are made in place per SPEC §5.2; it exists for wire-identical versions minted before that rule.

supersededBy.description: Successor reference for a `retired` specification, per SPEC §7.3 item 11. `<slug>` form points at the latest non-retired version of that slug; `<slug>/<MAJOR.MINOR>` pins to a specific version. The build script enforces that this field is only set when `status: retired`.

bearer.description: Opt-out from the audience-binding rule of SPEC §4.8.2. When true, documents conforming to this specification MAY omit `recipient` even when `proof` is present, because the payload's assertion is meaningful to any consumer that can verify the producer's identity (a public attestation, heartbeat, etc.). A bearer specification MUST also declare its `recipient` party as OPTIONAL. The default is false (non-bearer). See SPEC §4.8.3 and §7.3 item 12.
